newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS SMALL CAPS MARKET TECHNICALLY READY.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS SMALL CAPS MARKET TECHNICALLY READY.

text.p: Belgium's new small capitalisation market or "Nouveau Marche" which is on target for launch in January, is technically ready and its rules should be approved in December, the Brussels bourse said on Wednesday.

"The draft market rules will be approved by the end of the year - by the finance minister on the advice of the Belgian Banking and Finance Commission - and the market is technically ready...," Olivier Lefebvre, head of the Brussels bourse management committee told Reuters.
Companies had yet to formally apply for listing, but so far about half a dozen had shown serious interest, he added.
The market is being set up as part of the federation-style Euro-NM project, a rival to the pan-European growth stocks market Easdaq which saw its trading debut on Wednesday.
Under Euro-NM, individual bourses set up their own interconnecting markets for young companies seeking to raise capital to fund their growth plans.

So far four exchanges are participating. Paris set up its Nouveau March in March this year and Frankfurt, like Brussels, is due to launch a similar market in early 1997. The Amsterdam bourse says its small cap market will be operational in mid December and begin trading in the first half of 1997.
The participating exchanges aim to have an international marketing plan and harmonise their rules on market introductions.

Conditions for admission to the Brussels new market include 60 million Belgian francs of equity, and a minimum of 100,000 of securities to be distributed to the public which would be worth a minimum 100 million francs.

Companies can gain entry by introducing existing shares or by a capital increase whereby the newly created shares are quoted. If the company is less than two years old it can only be introduced by a capital increase.

A Belgian intermediary in the new market will be able to transmit orders from his office directly to the other new markets. Transactions will be conducted either via a central electronic order book or market making.
Lefebvre said the Euro-NM combined the strength of interest in the home market with an international dimension.
Easdaq and Euro-NM were "to some extent" competitors.
"We should not have a simplistic view - there is no pan-European reality," he said. "Our approach is probably more consistent with the European reality, which is the scenario of multi-access."
Lefebvre was speaking before a presentation at the Brussels bourse attended by several companies which said they were considering a Brussels Nouveau Marche listing.

These were Belgium Systemat SA, a global IT service provider for corporate clients; International Brachytherapy SA, involved in cancer treatment through radiation implants; Synergia Holdings, which takes majority stakes in building material, transport and equipment makers with growth potential to sell them later; and Ecopolis, an ecological glass waste collector.
Also present was U.K. sock firm Pex Plc Plc, quoted in London, and Belgian aluminium anodisation company Coil, already launched on the Paris nouveau marche.
